title: Separating a promise pair preserves NP-hardness
statement: Let $Y,N,L$ be languages of binary strings. Suppose $Y$ and $N$ are disjoint, and every language in NP has a polynomial-time map sending its members into $Y$ and its nonmembers into $N$. If $Y\subseteq L$ and $N\cap L=\varnothing$, then $L$ is NP-hard under polynomial-time many-one reductions.
hypotheses_covered: Every NP language has a polynomial-time promise reduction mapping members to $Y$ and nonmembers to $N$.
